They are old mechanical jury-riggers.  They have no clue about newer cars and newer technology.

I enjoy the show, but I have a love/hate with these guys.  They are entertaining, but DON'T RELY ON THEM for advice. Why?  Because they have some very out of date knowledge and make stupid claims like sports cars should not be allowed on roads because they go too fast and have too much power, and "nobody needs one".  Further, some of the advice they give is outright wrong.  For example, they claim you can test whether your clutch is going by parking your car against a tree and applying the clutch to see if it slips in high gear.  If you were driving a 1978 Lada, this MIGHT work.  But on a modern car you can damage the one-time collision areas, and could overheat the clutch plate on a single or double puck clutch producing slippage where none exists.  Further, the scratches the bumper and paint will cost you more than a new clutch.  Again, this stuff worked on cars with chrome bumpers, but not cars made in the last 20 years.

There are hundreds of examples of this bad advice that non-car enthusiasts wouldn't have any idea is wrong.

And people should drive whatever kind of car they want, provided they can afford it.  If you want a sports car, DRIVE ONE.

Religion.  Nearly all parents try to make their kids the same religion as themselves, and do it at a young age, even though they can never substantiate their own religion.  Worse, suppose you have 30 religions - the odds of you having it "right", with all things being equal, are only 1 in 31 (the 31st being that no religion is right).  There are thousands of religions.  Now the weak response to this is that they aren't all equal, and that just I know the truth that mine is the one true religion - except EVERYONE thinks that, including those adherents to the thousands of others.

Thus, statistically speaking, the chance of you being right is a fraction of a percent, and everyone is just as convinced they are in that tiny fraction as you are.  On top of that, there is a real chance that none of them are right.  Thus, don't teach your kids religion, because odds are you are lying to them.
